name: 208. Databricks OAuth M2M token-mint failures and fallback gating (databricks oauth failure)
description:
Pins the client-visible failure behaviour of Databricks OAuth M2M after the provider moved onto the shared token cache (core/providers/utils/tokencache). Two shapes:

1. The workspace host is unreachable (127.0.0.1:9). The token mint gets no HTTP status, which is a temporary outage: the error allows fallbacks and the configured fallback serves the request (x-bifrost-routing-info-is-fallback: true).
2. The token endpoint answers 401 invalid_client. That is a credential or configuration fault: the error names the token endpoint, blocks fallbacks, and the request fails even though a fallback is configured. The answer comes from a local fixture so it cannot drift to a 429 or 5xx, which would correctly be treated as transient: start node tests/e2e/api/runners/databricks-token-fixture.mjs (port 8795, override with --port and the databricksTokenFixtureUrl variable) and run with INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1. The row creates the provider with proxy_config pointing at the fixture and trusting the CA it serves at /__ca.

Databricks is not a supported base for custom providers, so both cases configure the built-in databricks provider itself through the management API (create the provider, then add a key through /keys, since inline keys on provider creation are ignored) with a bogus service principal, so no Databricks credential is needed, and delete it afterwards. Setup refuses to run over an operator-configured databricks provider; only a leftover carrying the harness key name is replaced. Case 2 carries [EXPECT-401] because the token endpoint's status is passed through to the client, which the collection-level status test must expect. Before the shared cache, every mint failure allowed fallbacks, so case 2 served from the fallback; it is the red-before pin for the new gating. The secret must never appear in a response body.

Run with FEATURE="databricks oauth failure".
